Database handbook (public, investigator supplied from pinned build and migration code).
Three groups: g1=office products, g2=electronics, g3=musical instruments.
Use normalized TEMP VIEW products(category,ref_id,title,price,catalog_rating,status,image_count),
reviews(category,ref_id,product_id,user_id,rating,body,review_date,year,month,verified,verification_label,epoch_seconds),
attributes(category,ref_id,attr_key,attr_val), categories(category,ref_id,cat_lvl,cat_nm).
Prices are dollars in the views. epoch_seconds retains numeric epoch timestamps, including corrupt very large values. SQLite date/year return NULL outside their supported range; compare epoch_seconds for far-future checks. Join views on BOTH category and ref_id. Do not join
reviews.product_id to products: ref_id is the foreign key. Review rows, products,
attribute lines and distinct users are different counting units. A product can have
many reviews and attributes. Taxonomy level 0 is department, level 1 is broad category.
Don't use catalog_rating when asked for actual mean of review ratings. Do not exclude
archived products unless the question requests active products. Attribute values
are original strings; SQL can inspect keys/values. g2 has no attributes, g3 no taxonomy.
Raw tables remain available: items_gN, fdbk_gN, taxn_g1/g2, attrs_g1 and original attrs_g3.
Raw ttl=title, prc=price, rtg=rating, avg_rtg=catalog rating, uid=user, ts=timestamp,
ref_id=product foreign key, vrf=verified. Original g1: dollars, epoch milliseconds,
integer vrf 0/1. g2: integer cents, epoch seconds, text vrf 'true'/'false'. g3: dollars,
ISO date text, integer vrf. fdbk_stats_g1 is an incomplete precomputed table; don't
substitute it for all actual reviews. items_g2.prc_usd is biased; do not use it.

matches.question: What is the average listed price of electronics products, expressed in dollars?
matches.sql: SELECT AVG(price) FROM products WHERE category = 'electronics'

matches.question: Among electronics reviews with a review body longer than 500 characters, considering only products whose list price is at most $40, what percentage are 1-star? Round to 2 decimal places.
matches.sql: SELECT CAST(222 AS REAL) * 100 / 2172 AS percentage

matches.question: Among electronics products that have zero reviews, what percentage have a price listed (non-NULL, non-zero)? Round to 2 decimal places.
matches.sql: SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN price IS NOT NULL AND price > 0 THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE category = 'electronics' AND ref_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT ref_id FROM reviews WHERE category = 'electronics')

messages.content:
Complete the database report with a correct executable SQL query. One JSON tool action per turn, no prose.
You have read-only SQLite, retained SQL and exact source histories. Use ordinary execution to check your work; public SQL errors are repair feedback, not correctness labels. Search relevant retained experience when useful. Current documentation overrides old examples.
Normalized views are installed automatically:
products(category,ref_id,title,price,catalog_rating,status,image_count)
reviews(category,ref_id,product_id,user_id,rating,body,review_date,year,month,verified,verification_label,epoch_seconds)
attributes(category,ref_id,attr_key,attr_val); categories(category,ref_id,cat_lvl,cat_nm).
category is 'office products', 'electronics', or 'musical instruments'. price is DOLLARS; verified is integer 0/1. Join views on category AND ref_id. product_id is NOT the product foreign key. category taxonomy level1 is broad category. Count the requested unit (reviews/products/distinct users), not joined duplicates. For a count of products satisfying a GROUP BY/HAVING condition, count the grouped rows with an outer SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (...); do not output one count per product. Do not confuse catalog_rating with actual review means. Do not drop archived products unless requested. NULL text verification_label means missing label, NOT unverified. Use year/month for available date parts. SQLite dates/years can be NULL for huge corrupt epochs; use numeric epoch_seconds to test far-future timestamps. Raw tables are also available; inspect schemas/docs when needed.
Tools:
{"tool":"sql","query":"SELECT ..."} executes a read-only query, returns up to 20 preview rows.
{"tool":"submit","query":"SELECT ..."} executes final SQL and writes the FULL result to answer.json. Use exactly the requested result/column(s). It does not grade correctness.
{"tool":"schema"} lists all raw and view columns. Optional table name selects one.
{"tool":"read","name":"documentation.txt"} reads handbook. name="views.py" reads helper implementation.
{"tool":"search_history","query":"your current need"} returns the 3 most relevant retained questions and executable SQL, with source IDs.
{"tool":"read_source","id":"source-id","index":0} reads an exact training record (messages and target); omit index to list metadata and record counts.
{"tool":"run_saved","id":"source-id","params":{}} executes retained SQL and writes answer.json. This is direct reuse, not query regeneration. Params optional.
{"tool":"save_sql","name":"name","query":"SELECT ..."} retains a query in this job; run_saved may use its name. Useful successful source queries are inherited across sessions by both conditions.
{"tool":"experience"} lists shared history metadata. After inspecting successful final execution emit exactly {"tool":"finish"}. Never finish after a failed submit. No evaluator labels are available.
Controller guidance:
There are 12 source queries available. Search the history for related work when useful; execute saved queries directly when they answer the current request.
Inherited artifacts available to environment tools: documentation.txt, history.json, views.py
